doc.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025

title: Demo musicians and the shift to the new rock feel
summary: Older swing guitarists gave way to younger players with the straight-eighth feel, which led her to record dates.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Were the musicians at that time normally able to say — I mean you could say to them, “You know this is in D, can we take it up in E flat it will sound better”? They were capable of that?

Yes. Oh yeah. And usually if they had a guy singer or something that they had to put it in a different key, I have perfect pitch and so it was like having to transpose each note as I sight read it. But the musicians were incredible. Because it was, you know, after the big band era and so the people that were with big bands — Everett Barksdale — do you remember that guitar player with Art Tatum? Everett did a lot of demos. And then as it went on the newer kids, Al Gorgoni and Trade Martin, the younger kids came in because when all the music started and all of the kids from Brooklyn came in, there’s a different © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
feel to it. And so the guitar players like Bucky and George and those people didn’t have that feel. So the new young kids were playing it.

You know Bucky talked about that, how some people could grab the — they call it the “straight eighth note feel” as opposed to swing. Some people could transition to it and some people couldn’t or didn’t want to.

Absolutely right. It all changed. And actually that’s how I got into doing record dates because I had — I didn’t come in as a jazz person, I didn’t ever listen to “Rock Around the Clock” and that stuff. But when I started doing the demos for Aldon Music mainly and Hill & Range, all of these that were the young writers and you know what the Carole King feel is, I could do that. And I didn’t laugh at it as some of the older singers and musicians did. And so everything really changed. And so I really became the hottest call to get singers in record dates because I could get singers that read. There were still written parts, but could get that feel.
